title: Burrowing Owl with moth
subtitle: A burrowing owl in low flight at Rocky Mountain Arsenal, Colorado, locked onto a moth in mid-air. Soft, uniform grass behind the bird sits alongside finely-detailed feather and face structure — giving noise-reduction tools both a smooth gradient region and a high-detail region to handle.
exif_summary: OM-1MarkII with OM 150-400mm F4.5 TC + MC-14 at 700mm, 1/2000s at f/8, ISO 6400

critique.text: The original RAW image is severely compromised by heavy, coarse noise that permeates the entire frame, significantly degrading both the subject and the background. Furthermore, the main subject (the owl) is quite soft, lacking fine detail in the feathers and facial features, likely due to slight motion blur or missed focus combined with the high noise floor. The other submitted images attempt to rescue this file with varying degrees of AI processing. Overall, the DxO PureRAW edit (Image 4) is the clear winner, flawlessly balancing noise reduction with natural detail recovery. Topaz (Image 1) takes second place, offering sharp details but with some minor artifacts. Lightroom (Image 5) effectively removes noise but leaves the subject soft, ranking third. The ON1 edit (Image 3) is the least effective, resulting in an unnatural texture.

images.title: DxO PureRAW 6
images.caption: DxO using DxO DeepPrime wD3 with Lens Sharpness Optimization increased to 150 (Strong)

critique.text: The DxO PureRAW 6 edit is exceptional and easily the best of the group. It completely eliminates the heavy noise of the original RAW file, leaving a perfectly smooth and natural-looking background. More impressively, the 'Strong' lens sharpness optimization successfully extracts incredible detail from the originally soft owl. The feathers, eyes, and talons are rendered crisply and naturally, entirely avoiding the over-sharpened, brittle artifacts seen in the Topaz version. It is a highly successful rescue of a very difficult, noisy, and soft original image.

images.title: Topaz Photo
images.caption: Topaz Photo with noise reduction and subject sharpening using default values

critique.text: The Topaz Photo edit significantly improves upon the original RAW by aggressively reducing noise and sharpening the subject. The background is much cleaner, though slight mottling remains. The subject sharpening effectively brings back missing detail in the owl's face and feathers, which is a major improvement. However, the sharpening effect is quite strong, resulting in a slightly 'crunchy' and over-processed look with minor artifacting along high-contrast edges. It's a strong rescue of a soft image, but it falls short of the natural rendering seen in the DxO edit.

images.title: Lightroom Denoise
images.caption: Lightroom AI Denoise at default settings

critique.text: The Lightroom AI Denoise version is very successful at its primary task: it completely cleans up the severe noise found in the original RAW, providing a smooth, distraction-free background without introducing strange artifacts. However, because it primarily addresses noise at default settings, the owl remains almost as soft as it was in the original file. Without the dedicated AI sharpening algorithms used by Topaz or DxO, the main subject lacks the crisp detail needed to make the image truly compelling. It is a very clean image, but the uncorrected softness holds it back.

images.title: ON1 RAW
images.caption: ON1 RAW with NoNoise and TackSharp

critique.text: The ON1 RAW edit struggles significantly with the source file. While it reduces the prominent noise of the RAW, it replaces it with a somewhat splotchy, unnatural texture in the out-of-focus background areas. The 'TackSharp' application on the owl fails to recover crisp details, instead producing a smudged, waxy, or 'plasticky' appearance that looks heavily digitally altered rather than naturally sharp. Compared to the original and the other edits, this version introduces unpleasant artifacts without successfully achieving the desired clarity.
